summary: Watch-only wallet export reopens a pathname after a non-atomic existence check and placeholder creation, allowing symlink substitution.
evidence: The authenticated exportwatchonlywallet RPC passes its destination pathname to ExportWatchOnlyWallet. That function checks fs::exists(destination), creates and closes a placeholder with std::ofstream, then performs substantial descriptor, wallet, and transaction-copy work before passing the same pathname to BackupWallet. The in-memory SQLite backend subsequently calls sqlite3_open(dest.c_str()) by name. A local attacker able to modify the destination directory can pre-place a dangling symlink (which passes the exists check) or replace the closed placeholder during the export window, redirecting the final SQLite write to another pathname with the node process's authority.
context: Reachability requires an RPC operator to export into a directory writable by a less-privileged local attacker. A private destination directory removes the cross-user boundary; shared-directory permissions and platform symlink protections determine practical impact.
